title: Equivariant resolution evaluation has the normalized derived bar arrow
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $G$ be a profinite group, and let $N$ be an internal $A$-module with trivial $G$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Use ordinary derived categories and derived invariants [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], with their canonical derived-functor unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write
$$R_N^n=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{n+1}],N),\qquad n\geq0,$$
where the internal Hom is underived, $A[X]$ is the free internal module on the condensed set $X$, and $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Give $R_N^n$ the diagonal action $(g\cdot f)(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=f(g^{-1}g_0,\ldots,g^{-1}g_n)$, the differential $\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i f(g_0,\ldots,\widehat{g_i},\ldots,g_{n+1})$, and the constant-function augmentation $N[0]\to R_N^\bullet$. All complexes here vanish in negative degrees. Let $a:N[0]\to K^\bullet$ be an equivariant quasi-isomorphism and let $e:K^\bullet\to R_N^\bullet$ be an equivariant cochain map whose composite with $a$ is the constant-function augmentation.

Put $U_N^n=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^n],N)$ with the trivial-action inhomogeneous bar differential. Invariant homogeneous functions identify with $U_N^n$ by
$$f\longmapsto\bigl[(g_1,\ldots,g_n)\longmapsto f(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n)\bigr].$$
Let $\rho:(K^\bullet)^G\to U_N^\bullet$ be the resulting cochain map from $e$. Write $j:U_N^\bullet\to\mathscr B_A(G;N)$ for the underived-to-derived bar map, and $\epsilon:R\Gamma_G(N[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B_A(G;N)$ for the normalized bar isomorphism of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. For $Q$ the localization at quasi-isomorphisms and $u_K:Q((K^\bullet)^G)\to R\Gamma_G(QK^\bullet)$ the canonical derived-invariants unit, the equality
$$j\circ Q(\rho)=\epsilon\circ(R\Gamma_G(Qa))^{-1}\circ u_K$$
holds in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$. No acyclicity of $K^n$ or of $R_N^n$ is assumed. The bar uses compatible nonnegative injective resolutions as in the cited bar node.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal E$ for internal $G$-equivariant modules, $\mathcal M$ for ordinary internal modules, $U$ for forgetting the action, and $F=\Gamma_G$. By the derived restriction calculus, both categories are Grothendieck abelian, $U$ is exact and detects exactness, and $F$ is additive and right adjoint to exact trivial inflation, hence left exact. Enough injectives gives a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $s:N[0]\to I^\bullet$: embed $N$ in an injective, embed its cokernel in the next injective, and continue. These successive embeddings make the augmented sequence exact. The cited K-injective computation theorem says $I^\bullet$ is K-injective.

proof.text: For a profinite parameter $S$, the free module $A[S]$ is $j_{S!}A_S$: maps from the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}A(V)$ to a module sheaf are determined by the image of the identity generator at $S$, so its sheafification has exactly the free universal property. The internal/section-module equivalence allows application of the cited flatness theorem; thus $A[G]$ is flat. The functor $L(M)=A[\underline G]\otimes_A M$, with translation on the first factor, is left adjoint to $U$: $h:M\to UJ$ corresponds to $[g]\otimes m\mapsto g h(m)$, with inverse evaluation at $[1]$. These formulas hold after every base change. Since $U$ creates exactness and tensor with $A[G]$ is exact, $L$ is exact. The exact-left-adjoint injectivity theorem now implies that $UI^q$ is injective for every $q$. Exactness of $U$ makes $Us$ an ordinary internal-module injective resolution.

proof.text: Form $T^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{p+1}],UI^q)$ for $p,q\geq0$, with homogeneous deletion differential horizontally and $d_I$ vertically. Give it the diagonal action on arguments AND the action on $I^q$ on values. These differentials are equivariant and commute. Put $T=\operatorname{Tot}T^{p,q}$ with $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$. The new homogeneous-function injectivity lemma applies to $I^q$, using step 2, so each $T^{p,q}$ is equivariantly injective. Each $T^n$ is a finite sum of these objects, hence injective: extend a map across a monomorphism separately after each of the finitely many projections, and take their sum into the finite biproduct. Thus $T$ is a bounded-below complex of equivariant injectives. There is an equivariant cochain map $\delta:I\to T$ placing the constant function with value $x\in I^q$ in bidegree $(0,q)$: its horizontal differential is zero and its vertical differential is the constant function with value $d_Ix$.

proof.text:
There is a cochain isomorphism $\chi:F(T)\to V$, where
$$V=\operatorname{Tot}_{p,q\geq0}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],UI^q)$$
has the inhomogeneous action differential. In bidegree $(p,q)$ take $f$ to $c(g_1,\ldots,g_p)=f(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_p)$; its inverse is
$$f(h_0,\ldots,h_p)=h_0\cdot c(h_0^{-1}h_1,h_1^{-1}h_2,\ldots,h_{p-1}^{-1}h_p).$$
Cancellation of the common left factor proves equivariance and that the formulas are inverse after every profinite base change. Deleting the first homogeneous coordinate gives $g_1c(g_2,\ldots)$, deleting an interior one multiplies the adjacent arguments, and deleting the last drops the last argument, with their original alternating signs. Postcomposition with $d_I$ commutes with evaluation because $d_I$ is equivariant. This proves the cochain assertion with the total signs of step 3. Invariants commute with these finite biproducts: a tuple is fixed exactly when each coordinate is fixed. Write $v=\chi F(\delta):F(I)\to V$; it is the bar-degree-zero inclusion of invariants.

proof.text:
Use $Us$ as the single compatible resolution for every derived internal Hom term. Step 2 makes this legitimate. The bar theorem, with the augmentation normalization specified in the bar-data node, identifies $QV$ with $\mathscr B_A(G;N)$ and gives
$$\epsilon=Q(v)\circ c_s,\qquad c_s=u_I^{-1}\circ R F(Qs):R F(QN)\longrightarrow QF(I).$$
Here $u_I$ is invertible since $I$ is K-injective. The formula for $c_s$ is the normalized derived-functor comparison, not a choice of an isomorphism on cohomology. In this model the underived-to-derived bar map $j$ is postcomposition with $s$ into the resolution-degree-zero row of $V$.

proof.text:
Define $t:R_N\to T$ in degree $p$ by postcomposing with $s^0:N\to UI^0$ and putting the result in bidegree $(p,0)$. It is a cochain map since $d_Is^0=0$, and is equivariant because $s$ is equivariant and $N$ is trivial. From the definition of $\rho$ and the coordinate formulas of step 4 one obtains the equality of cochain maps
$$\chi\circ F(t e)=j_{\mathrm{chain}}\circ\rho.$$
Indeed both send $x\in F(K^p)$ to the function $s^0(e^p(x)(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots))$ in bidegree $(p,0)$ and have zero other bidegree components. Here $j_{\mathrm{chain}}$ is the model of $j$ fixed in step 5.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of equivariant resolution-to-bar normalization

proof.text: The map $a$ is degreewise monic. In degree zero, since $K^{-1}=0$, its induced isomorphism $N=H^0(N[0])\to H^0(K)=\ker d_K^0$ shows that $a^0$ is a monomorphism; in other degrees the source is zero. Apply the cited lifting lemma to the monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $a:N[0]\to K$, the bounded-below injective complex $I$, and $s:N[0]\to I$. It gives an equivariant cochain map $b:K\to I$ with $ba=s$.

Both maps $te,\delta b:K\to T$ have the same composite with $a$. The first composite sends $n$ to the constant function with value $s^0(n)$ in bidegree $(0,0)$, because $ea$ is the given augmentation. The second is $\delta s$, the very same map. Since $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $T$ is bounded below with injective terms (step 3), the homotopy-uniqueness lemma gives $te\simeq\delta b$ equivariantly. Applying additive invariants to $te-\delta b=dH+Hd$ preserves this equation. Localization therefore gives
$$Q(\chi)\,QF(te)=Q(v)\,QF(b).$$

Naturality of the derived unit in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] gives
$$QF(b)=u_I^{-1}\circ R F(Qb)\circ u_K.$$
Since $ba=s$ and $Qa$ is invertible, functoriality gives $R F(Qb)=R F(Qs)\circ(R F(Qa))^{-1}$. Substitute this in step 8, and then use steps 5 and 6:
$$j\circ Q(\rho)=Q(v)\circ c_s\circ(R F(Qa))^{-1}\circ u_K=\epsilon\circ(R F(Qa))^{-1}\circ u_K.$$
Only $I$ and the auxiliary $T$ were required to have injective terms. In particular, this argument imposed no acyclicity condition on the given $K^n$ or $R_N^n$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-3c6872baf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all nine steps, the new node and the cited statements in full. On the base the item had an empty proof; it was created by Q06 on 2026-10-22 for the polynomial-bar node, so it is not a 2026-10-21 re-split and is not on the dropped list. No SGA is cited. Step-by-step checks: (1) Grothendieck abelian with enough injectives gives an equivariant injective resolution s:N[0]->I, which is K-injective by lem-sp-kinjective-computes (2). (2) A[S]=j_{S!}A_S by the universal property, so it is flat by 03EV (read). L=A[G](x)- with translation is an exact left adjoint of U, and its transpose formulas are correct. By 015Z (read), U preserves injectives. (3) T^{p,q}=Hom(A[G^{p+1}],UI^q) with diagonal and value action; its terms are injective by the new node, and finite biproducts of injectives are injective. delta is the constant function, and its horizontal differential x-x=0. (4) chi(f)=f(1,g1,g1g2,...) with inverse h0.c(h0^{-1}h1,...); I checked invariance and that the first face equals g1.c(g2,...), the bar-data first face. (5) eps=Q(v)c_s is exactly the bar-data computation datum, which is normalized by the total augmentation and is Assertion(G) of the bar node. j is modeled as postcomposition with s^0; it is a chain map since s^0 is equivariant and N is trivial. (6) t is a chain map since d_I s^0=0. It is equivariant because N is trivial. chi F(te)=j rho holds coordinatewise. (7) a^0 is monic because K^{-1}=0 gives H^0=ker d^0, which satisfies the hypothesis of the 013P(2) lift lemma (read). (8) te.a=delta.s=const s^0 n, so te and delta b are homotopic by 013S (read). (9) Unit naturality and RF(Qb)=RF(Qs)RF(Qa)^{-1} give the stated equality exactly, with no acyclicity of K^n or R_N^n used. New node lem-sfb-internal-homogeneous-functions-injective: it is true, since H_n(J) is isomorphic to the coinduction of Hom(A[G^n],UJ) (I checked the untwisting). Coinduction is right adjoint to the exact U, and Hom(A[G^n],UJ) is injective by flatness. Small cases: G=1 gives UJ (the hypothesis), n=0 gives the twisted coinduced module, and J=0 gives 0. It is statement-only, self-contained, and strictly smaller than the item. The rg -L duplicate search found no duplicate: the lem-exc-coinduced-* nodes are about discrete modules over finite rings, and lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution states exactness and the induced-module form, not injectivity. tool_uses (kinjective-computes, j-shriek-flat, tensor-closed, lift-unique-homotopy) are generic black-box homological tools and accepted. No fixes.
